title: Horde Fleet Connectivity
description: One screen for outage shapes: the WireGuard mesh, the edge's view of the backends, the backends' own logs, request telemetry, and the database host. Built after the 2026-09-08 aihdb01 partition.

options.content:
Each row is one vantage point on the same event. A **datastore partition** shows as handshake age climbing on the tunnel row, backend hosts dropping on the edge row, redis-unreachable lines on the backend row, and traffic piling onto the surviving host on the application row. A **sick database host** shows on the bottom row first (IO wait, load, latency) with the tunnel row flat. A **lost monitoring path** shows scrape status going red on several hosts while the edge row and app logs stay healthy. Firing critical alerts are drawn as annotations. Colors are fixed per host on every panel: troll blue, kobold orange, gremlin aqua, medusa yellow, stablehorde_orig magenta, aihdb01 green, orc violet, aihorde.net red.

**Overlays.** Every timeline carries the shared annotation set: infra and app alerts (chronic ones excluded), backend restarts (the INIT `Horde Database` line), and operator/deploy notes tagged `ai-horde` (`ops/scripts/annotate.sh`, the prod deploy play). Hover a marker before reading a line. **Edge row** is the user-impact view that does not depend on app telemetry; **Datastore: shared redis** needs the exporter from `docs/aihdb01-observability-manual.md` §6.

panels.title: Tunnel: WireGuard to the datastore host
Handshake age to aihdb01, seen from each backend
panels.description: A healthy tunnel with traffic re-keys about every 2 minutes. The line at 180 s is the WireGuardDatabasePeerStale threshold; two hosts above it is WireGuardDatabasePathPartitioned.

panels.title: Handshake age to each backend, seen from aihdb01
panels.description: The mirror image of the left panel. Both climbing: the path between them. Only this one climbing: aihdb01's own wg0 or host network (DatabaseHostTunnelPeersStale).

panels.title: Backend tunnel to aihdb01 (green = fresh handshake)
panels.description: One lane per backend. Red lanes are hosts whose redis and DB calls are failing.

panels.title: wg0 receive throughput per host
panels.description: Traffic collapsing to zero on a host means nothing is reaching it over the mesh; traffic doubling on one host means the edge has moved everyone else's load onto it.

panels.title: Client API: UP servers per backend host
panels.description: Stacked count of servers the edge considers UP, per backend host. A host's band vanishing is EdgeBackendHostDropped; the whole stack collapsing is EdgeBackendPoolEmpty.

panels.title: Worker API: UP servers per backend host
panels.description: Job dispatch goes through this backend. Fewer than 2 UP servers in total is EdgeWorkerApiCapacityLow (critical).

panels.title: Server UP/DOWN transitions per 5m, by backend
panels.description: Flapping shows here before it shows anywhere else. A burst across every backend at once is the edge losing its own path; one backend flapping is that backend's host.

panels.title: Edge health-check duration (p90 across servers)
panels.description: The heartbeat endpoint answers in tens of ms normally. It climbs toward the 2 s check timeout when backends are waiting on redis or the DB, before they go DOWN.

panels.title: Backends: what the app hosts see
Redis 'appears unreachable' log lines per minute, by host
panels.description: Each instance re-probes every 10 s, so a host with N instances logs ~6N lines per minute while the primary is down. Two hosts at once is HordeRedisUnreachableWidespread.

panels.title: Error and critical log lines per minute, by host
panels.description: The app's own view. A plateau of ~100/min on one host with the others quiet means that host's background timers are failing every tick.

panels.title: node_exporter scrape status from orc
panels.description: Three or more red lanes at once is orc's own upstream, not the hosts (MonitoringHostPartitioned). Compare with the edge row before believing an InstanceDown.

panels.title: 'Quorum changed' log lines per 5m
panels.description: Background-job quorum claims by non-owner nodes. A trickle is the redis fan-out stalling; a steady stream is the owner unable to renew the key.

panels.title: Application: request telemetry (hosts with OTLP enabled)
Requests per second by host
panels.description: Load redistribution is visible here: a surviving host's rate jumps as the edge sends it everyone else's traffic. Hosts without OTLP enabled are absent, not zero.

panels.title: p90 request duration by host
panels.description: Latency rising on every host together with the tunnel row flat points at the database host (see the bottom row), not the network.

panels.title: 5xx responses per second by host
panels.description: User-visible failures. Requests that hang until the edge times out never reach this counter, so read it together with the edge check duration.

panels.title: CPU by mode (share of all cores)
panels.description: IO wait above 25% for 10 minutes is DatabaseHostIoWaitHigh.

panels.title: Load per core (1m / 5m)
panels.description: Above 2 for 15 minutes is DatabaseHostLoadHigh.

panels.title: Memory available
panels.description: Under 10% for 10 minutes is DatabaseHostMemoryLow (critical): the OOM killer's next pick is a postgres backend.

panels.title: Disk read latency per operation, by device
panels.description: 50 ms per read sustained is DatabaseHostDiskLatencyHigh.

panels.title: Postgres connections
panels.description: Connection count climbing while requests/s falls means backends are stuck waiting, not busy.

panels.title: Longest open transaction
panels.description: A transaction holding locks for minutes serializes everything behind it.

panels.title: Edge: what users got (independent of app telemetry)
5xx responses per second, by edge host
panels.description: HAProxy's own count of 5xx responses on the public frontend. Includes 503s the edge generated itself when a backend pool was empty and 504s for requests that hung, neither of which reach the app's counters.

panels.title: 5xx share of responses, by edge host
panels.description: Same counter as a share of all responses on that edge. Baseline p99 is about 1% on stablehorde_orig and near zero on aihorde.net; EdgeFrontend5xxShareHigh fires at 5%.

panels.title: Requests per second, by edge host
panels.description: Total public-frontend request rate per edge. Traffic that vanishes here (rather than moving between backends) is a DNS/Cloudflare/edge problem, not a fleet one.

panels.title: Datastore: shared redis on aihdb01 (prometheus.exporter.redis via Alloy)
Redis up / clients
panels.description: redis_up from the exporter (0 = the exporter could not connect) and connected clients. Every backend instance holds several connections; a client count that collapses while redis_up stays 1 is the backends losing the tunnel, not redis dying.

panels.title: Redis memory
panels.description: Used memory against maxmemory (0 maxmemory = unlimited, shown as no line). Approaching the limit means evictions of the caches the app reads on every request.

panels.title: Redis commands per second
panels.description: Command throughput. A drop to near zero with the app still running is the fleet unable to reach redis; a spike is a cache stampede or a background job.

panels.title: Redis evictions, expirations, rejected connections (per 5m)
panels.description: Evictions mean memory pressure; rejected connections mean maxclients was hit (every backend instance reconnects at once after a partition heals).

panels.title: Redis keyspace hit ratio
panels.description: Hits / (hits + misses) over 5m. A sudden drop after a restart or flush is the cache rebuilding; a slow decline is keys expiring faster than the app refreshes them.

panels.title: Redis slowlog and latency
panels.description: Slowlog entries per 5m and the exporter's own ping round-trip; both rise when the host is IO-bound (see DatabaseHostIoWaitHigh) or a large key is being scanned.
